title: Isolation and Comparison of Neural Stem Cells from Adult Rat Brain and Spinal Cord
author: Schiro, Bauer, et al.
materials:
Timing: 1 h
33.1 day before starting EdU labeling: Prepare EdU kit solutions in accordance with protocol provided by supplier: (https://www.thermofisher.com/se/en/home/references/protocols/cell-and-tissue-analysis/protocols/click-it-edu-imaging-protocol.html).
CRITICAL: Ensure proper protective gear is worn when handling EdU as it interacts with DNA synthesis.
Timing: 1–3 h (depending on number of cultures)

steps.title: Prepare BSA and growth factor stocks
steps.instruction: Aliquot sterile 10 % BSA into 500 µL tubes, freeze at –20 °C. Dilute BSA to 0.1 % in sterile DPBS‑/‑. Reconstitute EGF and bFGF in this 0.1 % BSA to 10 µg mL⁻¹ (make 10 mL of each), aliquot and store at –20 °C (use within 7 days at 4 °C).

steps.title: Prepare CHIR 99021 stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve CHIR 99021 in DMSO to 10 mM, aliquot and store at –80 °C (stable ≤6 months; ≤1 month at –20 °C). Use aliquots within 7 days after thawing at 4 °C (e.g., 15 µL for one dissection).

steps.title: Set up dissection ice platform
steps.instruction: Fill a styrofoam box with crushed ice 2–3 cm above the top and flatten. Place a glass plate on the ice, cover with a 5–7 cm² piece of filter paper, and keep it moist with ice‑cold sterile saline just before animal anesthesia.

steps.title: Prepare transport and saline tubes
steps.instruction: For each niche to be extracted, fill a 15 mL conical tube with 10 mL Neurobasal 1× (label “transport + niche”) and keep on ice (≈90 % of tube covered). Fill another 15 mL tube with 12–14 mL sterile saline and keep on ice.

steps.title: Disinfect and arrange surgical tools
steps.instruction: Submerge all reusable instruments in disinfectant for ≥10 min (autoclave after each session). Prepare 5–7 cm² filter‑paper pieces, and set up the dissection table as illustrated (guillotine, glass plate, pipette, scissors, rongeurs, bone scissors, curved bone scissors, dissecting scissors, Heidemann spatula, hippocampal tool, Vannas spring scissors, Dumont #5 forceps, double‑sided razor blade, waste bag, OP‑towel, ice box, paper towels).

steps.title: Euthanize and expose brain
steps.instruction: Induce deep anesthesia with 4 % isoflurane, then decapitate. Disinfect animal, cut scalp, remove spinal column remnants, break open skull with rongeurs, cut skull open along the longitudinal fissure, lift dura with Heidemann spatula, and extract the brain with a curved hippocampal tool onto the ice‑cold glass plate, soaking in ice‑cold sterile saline.

steps.title: Dissect SGZ (dentate gyrus)
steps.instruction: Keep tissue chilled with ice‑cold saline. Remove cerebellum, split hemispheres sagittally with a chilled razor blade. Remove brain stem, cerebellum and basal ganglia to expose hippocampus. Halve hippocampus dorsoventrally, flip dorsal half onto filter paper, isolate dentate gyrus with spatula and forceps, discard CA regions, dice dentate gyrus on chilled razor blade, and transfer tissue to the transport tube containing ice‑cold Neurobasal 1×. Repeat for the second hemisphere.

steps.title: Dissect SVZ (lateral wall)
steps.instruction: Keep tissue chilled. Remove cerebellum, split hemispheres sagittally. Cut one hemisphere coronally 0.5 mm anterior to the hippocampal apex. Discard caudal part, trim basal ganglia and overhanging cortex to expose SVZ. Using Vannas spring scissors, cut the anterior 2/3 of the lateral SVZ as a thin sheet (uniform light‑brown color). Dice the sheet on chilled razor blade and transfer to the transport tube with ice‑cold Neurobasal 1×. Repeat for the second hemisphere.

steps.title: Dissect spinal cord and central canal
steps.instruction: Open chest and abdomen, remove internal organs. Cut spinal column at neck, release skin and ribs down to hips, cut spinal column rostral to rectus femoris. Cut each vertebra side‑by‑side with dissection scissors, douse exposed cord with ice‑cold saline. Grip rostral cord tip, cut dorsal root ganglia while lifting cord. Cut cord just below lumbar enlargement, place on chilled glass plate, douse with saline. Cut cord into 2–3 × 1 cm pieces with chilled razor blade. Remove lateral white matter with bone scissors, then dorsal white matter. Grab gray matter containing the central canal with fine forceps, cut it from ventral white matter, dice on chilled razor blade, and transfer to transport tube with ice‑cold Neurobasal 1×. Repeat for remaining pieces.

steps.title: Prepare dissociation reagents and media
steps.instruction: Make NSC base media (Table 1) and store at 4 °C ≤7 days. Prepare Resuspension and Expansion media for each niche (Tables 2‑4) and warm to 37 °C. Pre‑warm 12.5 mL unsupplemented Neurobasal 1× as wash media (37 °C). Disinfect a small styrofoam box, fill with crushed ice, spray with 70 % ethanol, and place in the laminar flow cabinet. Prepare a 15 mL tube with 11 mL HBSS‑/‑ (keep on ice). Warm accutase for CC and SVZ, and trypsin for SGZ, to 37 °C. Aliquot 10 µL of 0.4 % Trypan Blue in a sealed 0.5 mL tube. Have serological pipettes, an extra 15 mL tube and a cell‑counting chamber ready.

steps.title: Enzymatic tissue dissociation
steps.instruction: Spin transport tube at 100 × g for 1 min (RT 20–23 °C). Aspirate transport media, resuspend tissue in 5 mL ice‑cold HBSS‑/‑, spin again 100 × g 1 min (RT). Repeat the spin‑wash once more. Aspirate HBSS, add 1 mL accutase for CC or SVZ tissue, or 1 mL trypsin for SGZ tissue (at RT). Incubate 15 min (accutase) or 5 min (trypsin) at 37 °C. Triturate 500 times with a P100 or P200 set to 100 µL. Transfer dissociated tissue to a new 15 mL tube containing 1 mL warm wash media, rinse original tube with 1 mL warm Neurobasal 1× and add to the new tube, then add 2 mL Neurobasal 1× (final volume 5 mL). Spin at 150 × g 5 min (RT), aspirate, resuspend pellet in 4 mL warm wash media, spin again 150 × g 5 min, repeat wash once more.

steps.title: Count cells and seed initial culture
steps.instruction: Prepare a non‑tissue‑culture‑treated 6‑well plate (or appropriate plate) by adding 3.5 mL expansion media per well (recommended seeding density 5 × 10⁵ cells well⁻¹). Add 10 µL of cell suspension to 10 µL 0.4 % Trypan Blue, mix 10×, load 10 µL onto both sides of a counting chamber, count live cells (automatic counter or manual). Calculate volume containing 5 × 10⁵ live cells, add that volume to each well. Place plate in a humidified incubator (5 % CO₂, 37 °C) undisturbed for 4 days.

steps.title: First media change after dissociation
steps.instruction: After 4 days, prepare fresh base media (Table 1) supplemented with niche‑specific growth factors (Tables 2‑4) using small aliquots (store thawed aliquots ≤7 days at 4 °C; CHIR aliquots at –80 °C). Warm media to 37 °C. Remove 1 mL media from each well with a 5 mL serological pipette, triturate 2–3 times to detach adherent cells, transfer removed media to a 15 mL tube, triturate 3–4 times to break up neurospheres, then add 1 mL fresh warm media to the well. Repeat for all wells, centrifuge the collected tube at 150 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2 mL fresh media, triturate 3–4 times, and return to the original wells. Return plate to incubator.

steps.title: Passaging schedule and routine
steps.instruction: Suggested schedule: P0 – harvest day 0, media changes days 4 and 7, passage to P1 on day 10. P1 – media changes days 13, 16, 18, passage to P2 on day 20. Monitor phenol‑red color for acidification; adjust media change frequency as needed (P2 may need changes every 12–18 h).

steps.title: Passage NSCs (general procedure)
steps.instruction: For wells containing suspended neurospheres: remove media with a 5 mL serological pipette into an empty 15 mL tube, add 1 mL warm Neurobasal 1× to the well to keep adherent cells hydrated, then centrifuge the tube at 150 × g 5 min (RT). Aspirate supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL warm accutase (or trypsin) per well, triturate twice, add 1 mL dissociation agent back to the well, incubate 15 min (accutase) or 5 min (trypsin) at 37 °C, aspirate enzyme, wash well bottom with the enzyme solution, collect all cells into a 15 mL tube, triturate 100 times with a P200 (≈20 % of volume each pass). Add 4 mL warm Neurobasal 1× wash media (plus 1 mL per extra mL enzyme used), spin 150 × g 5 min, aspirate, resuspend in 4 mL warm wash media, spin again, repeat wash once more. Prepare new 6‑well plates (non‑treated for CC/SVZ, tissue‑treated for SGZ) with 3 mL culturing media per well, add 1 mL resuspended cells per well (adjust volume to deliver 5 × 10⁵ cells well⁻¹). Count a sample with Trypan Blue as above, then incubate plates (5 % CO₂, 37 °C). For wells without suspended cells: simply replace media with 1 mL dissociation agent per well and follow the same downstream steps.

steps.title: Coat coverslips with Poly‑L‑Ornithine
steps.instruction: Place one 13 mm glass coverslip in each well of a 24‑well plate, add 300 µL Poly‑L‑Ornithine solution, incubate 1 h at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C. Wash 3 × 5 min with sterile distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare Laminin coating solution
steps.instruction: On ice, mix 0.959 mL L‑15 media, 25 µL 0.9 M sodium bicarbonate (final 22.5 mM), 16 µL natural mouse laminin (1 mg mL⁻¹) to obtain 1 mL Laminin solution (final 16.5 µg mL⁻¹). Use immediately or store at 4 °C ≤24 h (keep cold to avoid gelation).

steps.title: Laminin coat coverslips
steps.instruction: Submerge the Poly‑L‑Ornithine‑treated coverslips in 1 mL Laminin solution, incubate 1 h at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C. Remove solution and add warm (37 °C) appropriate cell‑culture media before starting passage.

steps.title: EdU labeling of proliferating cells
steps.instruction: One day before labeling, prepare EdU kit solutions per supplier instructions. Dilute EdU 1:500 in cell media, replace 50 % of existing media with this mixture to achieve a final 1:1000 (≈10 µM) EdU concentration. Incubate cells 12–24 h.

steps.title: Fix cells with Glyoxal
steps.instruction: Prepare 3 % Glyoxal fixative fresh: 0.708 mL H₂O, 0.197 mL absolute ethanol, 0.078 mL 40 % Glyoxal, 7.8 µL acetic acid (total 1 mL). Submerge cells (≈300 µL per well of a 24‑well plate) for 15 min at RT. Remove fixative, wash twice with 1× PBS for 5 min each (increase PBS volume by 100 µL per wash). Plates may be stored in PBS at 4 °C up to 3 weeks (quality declines after 1 week).

steps.title: Immunostaining – day 1 (primary)
steps.instruction: Remove PBS, add 0.5 % Triton‑X 100 in 1× PBS for 5 min. Wash twice 5 min with 1× PBS (increase volume each wash). Block with 5 % goat serum in 1× PBS (≈300 µL per well) for 1 h at RT. Prepare primary antibodies in 5 % goat serum, add to wells, incubate overnight (18–22 h) at 4 °C on a shaker. Include a well with no primary antibody as a control.

steps.title: Immunostaining – day 2 (secondary & Hoechst)
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibodies 1:500 in 5 % goat serum in 1× PBS, centrifuge 2 000 × g 15 min, keep supernatant. Wash wells 3 × 5 min with 1× PBS. Add secondary solution, place on low‑speed shaker for 3 h protected from light. During the last 30 min, prepare Hoechst 1:2000 in 1× PBS (protected from light). After secondary incubation, replace with Hoechst solution for 30 min. Wash 3 × 5 min with 1× PBS, then once with MQ water, replace with fresh MQ water (≈700 µL per well).

steps.title: Mount coverslips for imaging
steps.instruction: Place a drop of ProLong Gold Antifade mounting medium on a clean microscope slide, gently lift each coverslip with Dumont #5/90 curved forceps, tap one edge on tissue paper to remove excess liquid, lower coverslip onto mounting medium avoiding bubbles, seal edges with clear (non‑colored) nail varnish. Let dry 20–30 min, then an additional 15–20 min before imaging. Verify dryness by touching with filter paper (no imprint).

steps.title: Differentiate NSCs (≥15 days)
steps.instruction: Seed cells onto PLO‑Laminin‑coated 13 mm coverslips at densities from Table 6 (e.g., 5 × 10⁵ cells well⁻¹ for 6‑well). Expand for 3 days in supplemented expansion media (Tables 9‑10). Then replace with differentiation base media (Table 9) supplemented with BDNF (10 ng mL⁻¹) and FBS (1:1000). Change differentiation media every 3 days, keep cells for a minimum of 15 days before downstream analysis.

steps.title: Optional: Freeze‑thaw NSCs
steps.instruction: Follow established freezing and thawing protocols (e.g., 10 % DMSO in FBS, controlled‑rate freezing, storage in liquid nitrogen; thaw rapidly at 37 °C, dilute in warm media).

steps.title: Optional: Prepare cells for SEM
steps.instruction: Refer to external SEM preparation protocols; typically involves fixation, dehydration through graded ethanol series, critical‑point drying, and sputter coating.

description:
Timing: 1–2 h
CRITICAL: This protocol is optimized for NSC harvest from 10-week-old female Sprague Dawley rats for each of the three neurogenic niches; the subventricular zone (SVZ) and subgranular zone (SGZ) in the brain, and the central canal (CC) of the spinal cord. The principles described in this protocol can be used for other rat strains, gender, and ages, however, the yields of viable NSCs may somewhat vary. This protocol is optimized for the extraction of a single neurogenic niche per animal. However, we have also included guidance about how to extract both brain neurogenic niches (SVZ and SGZ) from the same animal. We do not however recommend extracting all three neurogenic niches from the same animal or extracting the CC in addition to either of the brain neurogenic niches (SVZ or SGZ) due to the impact of time-consuming procedures, i.e., euthanasia, dissection, and tissue extraction, on cell viability.1.Aliquot sterile 10% Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) solution into 500 μL aliquots for use in step 2. Freeze unused aliquots at −20°C.Note: Depending on the manufacturer, frozen BSA may be stable up to 24 months, see manufacturer’s instructions/certificate of analysis (CoA) of the particular batch.2.Dilute 10% BSA in sterile DPBS −/− to a concentration on 0.1% BSA.a.Reconstitute Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF) and Fibroblast Growth Factor-basic (bFGF) using this 0.1% BSA solution, both to a concentration of 10 μg/mL, up to a total of 10 mL of each solution.b.Aliquot and store at −20°C.Note: Using a 0.1% BSA solution is recommended at this concentration. Check the recommended reconstitution buffer and carrier protein for dilution to lower concentrations on the manufacturer’s instructions/CoA for the particular batch of growth factor being used.
